angle_en: Sanatana, the eternal seed of all beings

en.intro: Krishna has just shown that he is the fragrance in the earth and the radiance in fire. Now he names his own origin. Listen for the source he names for all beings and for the qualities he holds in people.
en.notice: He calls himself the seed, sanatana, eternal, of all beings, and then says he is the intelligence in the intelligent and the brilliance in the brilliant, so every clear mind and bright strength comes from him.
en.next: He now moves from the source of life to the source of strength, naming what he is in those who are strong.
en.meaning: Know Me, O Partha, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the brilliance of the brilliant.

hi.intro: कृष्णा ने अभी बताया है कि वे धरती में सुगंध और अग्नि में तेज हैं। अब वे अपने मूल रूप को बताते हैं। सुनिए, वे सभी प्राणियों के मूल को और लोगों में मौजूद किन गुणों को कहते हैं।
hi.meaning: हे पृथानन्दन, सम्पूर्ण प्राणियों का अनादि बीज मुझे जान। बुद्धिमानों में बुद्धि और तेजस्वियों में तेज मैं हूँ।
hi.notice: वे स्वयं को सभी प्राणियों का सनातन, यानी अनादि बीज कहते हैं, और फिर कहते हैं कि बुद्धिमानों में बुद्धि और तेजस्वियों में तेज वे स्वयं हैं, अतः हर स्पष्ट मन और तेज शक्ति उन्हीं से आती है।
hi.next: अब वे जीवन के स्रोत से शक्ति के स्रोत की ओर बढ़ते हैं, और बताते हैं कि वे बलवानों में क्या हैं।

issues: wrong_fact: "He calls himself the seed, sanatana, eternal, of all beings" (The intro and notice incorrectly state that Krishna calls himself the 'seed, sanatana, eternal, of all beings'. The Sanskrit source says 'sanatana' is the eternal seed, not that he calls himself 'sanatana'. He calls himself the 'eternal seed', not 'seed, eternal' as separate descriptors. The Hindi translation 'अनादि बीज' (beginningless seed) is supported by the Sanskrit 'sanatana', but the English notice breaks this into 'seed, sanatana' which is a factual misrepresentation of the source.)

unsupported: "Listen for the three things he says he is" (The source verse only explicitly mentions three things he is: the eternal seed, the intelligence of the intelligent, and the brilliance of the brilliant. However, the intro claims he will name 'three things', which is a factual claim about the content of the verse that is not explicitly stated in the source or standard interpretations. The verse itself is a direct statement, not a prompt to listen for three things.)
